title: Fact Sheet on Voter Deletion Patterns in the West Bengal Special Intensive Revision (SIR), 2025–26
shows: Reading 91 lakh elector records, it finds women were 53.6% of the 58 lakh names deleted in December 2025 and that in Nandigram, where Muslims are about a quarter of the population, they were 95% of the names deleted from the supplementary lists.

title: SIR redraws Bengal’s margins of power
shows: It finds the names deleted in West Bengal's revision outnumbered the winning margin in 161 of 293 Assembly seats, and still did so in 124 seats once deaths are left out.

title: Hyderabad SIR: 19.4 Lakh Electoral Roll Deletions Across 15 Assembly Seats
shows: It counts 19.41 lakh names deleted across Hyderabad's 15 Assembly seats, 46.1% of the January 2023 roll, more than the 2023 winning margin in every seat.

title: SIR Delhi 2026: The Excluded Roll and the 2025 Verdict
shows: Across all 14,947 polling parts it counts 47,56,722 uncollectable enumeration forms, 32.8% of Delhi's electorate, more than the 2025 winning margin in 68 of 70 seats.

title: Comprehensive Analysis of ASDD Deletions in Uttarakhand under the Special Intensive Revision of Electoral Rolls, 2026
shows: It finds at least 8,07,410 names on Uttarakhand's ASDD lists, 52.0% of them women and 57.7% recorded as permanently shifted, more than the 2022 winning margin in 45 of 70 seats.

title: SIR Manipur 2026: Preliminary Report on Electoral Roll Deletions
shows: Of the 1,58,677 names removed in Manipur, the 20 hill seats account for 66.4% and women for 55.96%, and women are the majority of those removed in all 60 seats.

title: Preliminary Report on SIR Meghalaya : State-wide analysis of all 60 Assembly Constituencies
shows: It finds 1,80,402 names on Meghalaya's ASDD lists, 8.32% of the roll, with death the largest recorded reason at 45.2% and the count above the 2023 winning margin in 32 of 60 seats.

title: Citizen’s Handbook for Filing SIR Voter Deletion Appeals
shows: It is a step-by-step guide to appealing a deletion from West Bengal's roll before the 19 appellate tribunals set up after the Supreme Court's order, with sample appeals for nine common situations.

title: Karnataka SIR 2026: Preliminary Report on Electoral Roll Deletions
shows: From the lists of names left off Karnataka's draft roll of 24 August 2026 for all 224 constituencies, the Sabar Institute counts 1,08,24,651 names with a recorded reason, which it puts at 20.4% of the 2023 roll. It finds 15.1% marked dead, and it describes the other 91,85,436, marked shifted, untraceable or absent, already enrolled elsewhere or as having refused the form, as alive. It reports that Bengaluru Urban has 18% of the state's electors and 44% of the names, and that in Bommanahalli, C.V. Raman Nagar, Dasarahalli, B.T.M. Layout and Vijay Nagar more names were left off than votes were cast in 2023. It finds 2,102 of the 4,926 third gender electors on the 2023 roll, 42.7%, on the lists. Among electors aged 18 to 29 marked a reason other than death it counts about three women for every two men, and nearly two for one outside Bengaluru. Outside Bengaluru Urban, by its correlations, districts with more Scheduled Caste residents and districts with lower income per head had more names left off.
